name: c23_tools_v1
prompt: Three square ancient Chinese bronze plaques side by side in one horizontal row with clear gaps between them, each the same size and style as the reference plaque (aged dark bronze with verdigris patina, raised rim border, four round rivets in the corners), seen straight on, flat frontal view. Each plaque has a different pictorial image deeply engraved (intaglio, carved grooves with dark recesses and worn bright bevel edges) in the style of Han dynasty stone relief carvings, NO text, NO letters, NO characters: LEFT plaque: a traditional Chinese drafting compass (gui) drawn as a real tool — a round hinge knob at top, two long tapering wooden-and-bronze legs spreading apart, one leg ending in a sharp point and the other holding an ink brush tip, with a carved circular arc traced around it. MIDDLE plaque: a Chinese carpenter's try-square (ju), a thick L-shaped bronze ruler lying diagonally at 45 degrees, with fine graduation tick marks along both arms and a small hanging ring at the corner. RIGHT plaque: an ancient Chinese steelyard balance scale, a vertical post with a horizontal beam and two round pans hanging on chains, perfectly level. Engravings are detailed, ornate, clearly pictorial objects, filling about 70% of each plaque. Even soft studio light from upper left. Isolated on a flat solid pure chroma green #00FF00 background, nothing else.
